description: Recommends transferring $766,300 to the Special Events Reserve.
Recommends limiting special event applications for 2026 and 2027.
Administration to report on future event funding by 2028.

chips.text: City Manager Jorgensen strongly disagreed with Discover Saskatoon's claims about the city's agility.
Discover Saskatoon advocated for strategic event funding and partnership.
Mayor Block questioned if the city could remain agile for quick event decisions.
Discover Saskatoon highlighted that public disclosure of bids weakens Saskatoon's competitiveness.
Administration will report on how other cities structure special event funding programs.

description: Approved 2026 cash grants for environmental community groups.
Committee recommends approving servicing agreement for North Marquis GP Ltd.
Agreement enables new industrial development in Marquis Industrial Area.
Development is for Parcel C, NW   Section 21.
Committee recommends developing a city land policy for affordable housing.
Policy would guide land disposition and acquisition processes.
Policy would ensure long-term affordability for projects.

chips.text: Chair emphasized importance of long-term affordability in the new policy.
New policy replaces current ad hoc approach to city land for housing.
No conclusive research guides long-term affordable housing expiry dates.
Métis Nation–Saskatchewan strongly supports the proposed land policy.
Policy would prioritize land sales to Indigenous-led developers.
Administration will develop the policy and bring it back for approval.

speakers.name: Lesley Anderson
speakers.summary: Lesley Anderson, Director of Planning and Development presented the report and responded to questions of the Committee related to the policy, long term affordability and community impact.
said: Policy provides a deliberate, long-term approach to securing affordable housing land.
It reduces upfront land costs and strengthens city's funding position.
Key elements include inventory, council approval, Indigenous priority, and development-ready sites.

description: Committee recommends RFP for Farmer's Market Building management.
RFP includes 120 Sonnenschein Way as optional component.
Prioritize proposals enhancing market success and community benefit.

chips.text: Administration clarified structured incubator programming ceased some time ago.
Tenants and vendors at Gather Local Market and 120 Sonnenschein Way.
Tenants of 120 Sonnenschein Way were not consulted for the report.
Delegates expressed strong support for the market's community and incubation services.
Negotiations underway with 57 black-owned startup businesses for market participation.
